sentences.zh: 〈（乙邦才馬應魁莊子固）〉

translations.literal: (Yi Bangcai; Ma Yingkui; Zhuang Zigu)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Sub-biographies: Yi Bangcai, Ma Yingkui, and Zhuang Zigu)〉

sentences.zh: 金國鳳，宣府人。

translations.literal: Jin Guofeng was a man of Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Guofeng was a native of Xuanfu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中，以副總兵守松山。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen reign, as vice commander he defended Songshan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongzhen era he served as vice commander and garrisoned Songshan.

sentences.zh: 十二年二月，大清以重兵來攻，環城發炮，臺堞俱摧。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twelfth year, Great Qing came with a heavy force to attack; they ringed the city and fired cannon, and the parapets were all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the twelfth year (1639), the Qing attacked in force, encircled the city, and bombarded it until the battlements were shattered.

sentences.zh: 城中人負扉以行。

translations.literal: The people in the city carried door panels to move about.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the city people had to carry door panels as shields when they moved about.

sentences.zh: 國鳳間出兵突擊，輒敗還，乃以木石甃補城壞處。

translations.literal: Guofeng from time to time sent troops out in sudden strikes, but each time was defeated and driven back; he then used timber and stone to face and repair the damaged places in the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Guofeng made repeated sorties, but each was beaten back; he then patched the breaches with timber and stone.

sentences.zh: 大清兵屢登屢卻，遂分兵攻塔山、連山，令銳卒分道穴城。

translations.literal: Great Qing troops repeatedly climbed [the wall] and were repeatedly driven back; they then divided forces to attack Tashan and Lianshan, and ordered elite soldiers to tunnel into the city by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: Qing troops stormed the walls again and again only to be repulsed; they then split forces against Tashan and Lianshan and sent picked men to mine under the walls along several routes.

sentences.zh: 國鳳多方拒守，終不下，閱四旬圍解。

translations.literal: Guofeng on many sides resisted and held; in the end [the city] did not fall, and after forty days the siege was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Guofeng held on by every means, and the city never fell; after forty days the siege was raised.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，立擢署都督僉事，為寧遠團練總兵官。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and at once promoted him to acting Regional Military Commissioner, making him commander of the Ningyuan militia regiment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and immediately promoted him to acting Regional Military Commissioner and appointed him commander of the Ningyuan militia regiment.

sentences.zh: 再論功，署都督同知，蔭錦衣衛千戶。

translations.literal: When his merit was discussed again, he was given acting rank as Chief Regional Military Commissioner and hereditary enrollment as a thousand-household in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On a further review of his service he was made acting Chief Regional Military Commissioner, with hereditary enrollment as a thousand-household in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 是年十月，大清兵復攻寧遠。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year, Great Qing troops again attacked Ningyuan.
translations.idiomatic: That October the Qing attacked Ningyuan again.

sentences.zh: 國鳳憤將士恇怯，率親丁數十人出據北山岡鏖戰。

translations.literal: Guofeng, angry that the officers and soldiers were timid, led several dozen of his personal retainers out to hold the northern hill ridge and fight a bitter battle.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged at his troops’ cowardice, Guofeng led several dozen household retainers out to hold the northern hill ridge and fight hand to hand.

sentences.zh: 移時矢盡力竭，與二子俱死。

translations.literal: After a while arrows were exhausted and strength spent; he and his two sons all died.
translations.idiomatic: When his arrows were spent and his strength gone, he and his two sons died together.

sentences.zh: 帝聞痛悼，贈特進榮祿大夫，左都督，賜祭葬，有司建祠，增世職三級。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he grieved deeply and posthumously granted him Grand Mentor of the Court with the title of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Left Chief Regional Military Commissioner, bestowed sacrificial rites and burial honors, ordered the local authorities to build a shrine, and increased his hereditary rank by three grades.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him deeply, posthumously granting him Grand Mentor of the Court with the title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Left Chief Regional Military Commissioner, with state sacrifices and burial, a shrine built by the local authorities, and an increase of three grades in hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 總督洪承疇上言：「國鳳素懷忠勇。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Hong Chengchou memorialized: "Guofeng has long cherished loyalty and courage.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Hong Chengchou wrote: "Guofeng has always been loyal and brave.

sentences.zh: 前守松山，兵不滿三千，乃能力抗強敵，卒保孤城。

translations.literal: Previously when he defended Songshan his troops were fewer than three thousand, yet he was able to resist a strong enemy with force and in the end preserve the isolated city.
translations.idiomatic: When he held Songshan before, he had fewer than three thousand men, yet he held off a powerful enemy and kept that isolated city.

sentences.zh: 非其才力優也，以事權專，號令一，而人心肅也。

translations.literal: It was not that his talent and strength were superior, but because his authority over affairs was undivided, orders were unified, and the hearts of men were stern.
translations.idiomatic: That was not because his talent exceeded others’, but because he held sole authority, orders were uniform, and the men were disciplined.

sentences.zh: 迨擢任大將，兵近萬人，反致隕命。

translations.literal: When he was promoted to great general with troops approaching ten thousand, he on the contrary met death.
translations.idiomatic: Once he was raised to full regional command with nearly ten thousand men under him, he lost his life instead.

sentences.zh: 非其才力短也，由營伍紛紜，號令難施，而人心不一也。

translations.literal: It was not that his talent and strength were deficient, but because the camps were in disorder, orders were hard to enforce, and the hearts of men were not one.
translations.idiomatic: That was not because his ability fell short, but because the camps were chaotic, orders could not be enforced, and the men were divided.

sentences.zh: 乞自今設連營節制之法，凡遇警守城，及統兵出戰，惟總兵官令是聽。

translations.literal: I beg that from now on a method of joint-camp regulation be established: whenever there is an alarm to hold a city, and whenever one commands troops out to battle, only the regional commander’s orders shall be obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that hereafter a system of joint-camp command be adopted: in any alert to hold a city or to take the field, only the regional commander’s orders shall be followed.

sentences.zh: 庶軍心齊肅，戰守有資，所系於封疆甚大。」

translations.literal: Then the hearts of the army may be united and stern, and attack and defense will have resources; what is bound up with the frontier is very great."
translations.idiomatic: Then the army will be united and disciplined, attack and defense will be effective, and the security of the frontier will be greatly strengthened."

sentences.zh: 帝即允行之。

translations.literal: The emperor at once approved and carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved at once.

sentences.zh: 及國鳳父子柩歸，帝念其忠，命所過有司給以舟車，且加二祭。

translations.literal: When the coffins of Guofeng and his sons returned, the emperor, mindful of their loyalty, ordered the authorities along the route to provide boats and carts, and added two further sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When the coffins of Guofeng and his sons were brought home, the emperor, remembering their loyalty, ordered officials along the route to supply boats and carts and granted two additional sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 其妻張氏援劉綎例，乞加宮保。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Zhang cited the precedent of Liu Ting and begged that he be given the honorary title of Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, Lady Zhang, cited the precedent of Liu Ting and asked that he be granted the honorary title of Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 部議格不行，而請於世職增級外，再蔭本衛試百戶世襲，以勸忠臣。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated and rejected it, but requested that beyond the increase in hereditary rank, there be a further hereditary enrollment as probationary hundred-household in his original guard, to encourage loyal ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry rejected that, but asked that in addition to raising his hereditary rank, a further hereditary probationary hundred-household in his original guard be granted to encourage loyal ministers.

sentences.zh: 帝可之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 當松山被圍，巡撫方一藻議遣兵救援，諸將莫敢應。

translations.literal: When Songshan was besieged, Grand Coordinator Fang Yizao proposed sending troops to relieve it, but none of the generals dared respond.
translations.idiomatic: When Songshan was besieged, Grand Coordinator Fang Yizao proposed a relief force, but none of the generals would volunteer.

sentences.zh: 獨副將楊振請行，至呂洪山遇伏，一軍盡覆。

translations.literal: Only Vice Commander Yang Zhen asked to go; when he reached Lühong Mountain he met an ambush and the whole army was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Only Vice Commander Yang Zhen offered to go; at Lühong Mountain he ran into an ambush and his entire force was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 振被執，令往松山說降。

translations.literal: Zhen was captured and ordered to go to Songshan to urge surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was taken prisoner and ordered to go to Songshan to urge surrender.

sentences.zh: 未至里許，踞地南向坐，語從官李祿曰：「為我告城中人堅守，援軍即日至矣。」

translations.literal: Before he had gone a full li, he sat on the ground facing south and said to his attendant Li Lu: "Tell the people in the city to hold firm; the relief army will arrive within the day."
translations.idiomatic: Before he had gone a full li he sat on the ground facing south and said to his attendant Li Lu, "Tell the men in the city to hold firm—the relief army will be here today."

sentences.zh: 祿詣城下致振語，城中守益堅。

translations.literal: Lu went to the foot of the city and delivered Zhen’s words, and the defenders in the city held all the more firmly.
translations.idiomatic: Li Lu went to the foot of the wall and delivered Zhen’s message, and the garrison held all the firmer.

sentences.zh: 振、祿皆被殺。

translations.literal: Zhen and Lu were both killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen and Lu were both put to death.

sentences.zh: 事聞，命優恤。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the court ordered generous condolence grants.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, generous posthumous honors were ordered.

sentences.zh: 振，義州衛人。

translations.literal: Zhen was a man of Yizhou Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was a native of Yizhou Guard.

sentences.zh: 世為本衛指揮使。

translations.literal: For generations his family had been commanders of that guard.
translations.idiomatic: His family had held the hereditary command of that guard for generations.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年，河東失守，歸路梗，其母自縊。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi, when the east of the [Liao] river was lost and the return route was blocked, his mother hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianqi (1622), when the territory east of the river was lost and the road home cut off, his mother hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 振隨父及弟夜行晝伏，渡鴨綠江入皮島。

translations.literal: Zhen followed his father and younger brother, traveling by night and hiding by day, crossed the Yalu River, and entered Pidao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen went with his father and younger brother by night marches and daytime concealment, crossed the Yalu, and reached Pidao.

sentences.zh: 毛文龍知其父子才，並署軍職。

translations.literal: Mao Wenlong knew the talent of father and son and both were given military posts.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Wenlong recognized their ability and gave father and son military appointments.

sentences.zh: 文龍死，振歸袁崇煥，為寧遠千總。

translations.literal: When Wenlong died, Zhen entered Yuan Chonghuan’s service as a thousand-household at Ningyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Wenlong’s death Zhen joined Yuan Chonghuan and served as a thousand-household at Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年從入衛。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongzhen he followed [the army] into the capital guard region.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chongzhen (1629) he marched into the metropolitan defense zone.

sentences.zh: 救開平有功，進都司僉書。

translations.literal: For saving Kaiping he had merit and was promoted to Assistant Commander in the Chief Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Assistant Commander in the Chief Military Commission for relieving Kaiping.

sentences.zh: 郵馬山之戰，以遊擊進參將。

translations.literal: In the battle at Youmashan he was advanced from mobile corps commander to vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Youmashan he was promoted from mobile corps commander to vice commander.

sentences.zh: 久之，擢副總兵。

translations.literal: After a long time he was promoted to vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was made vice commander.

sentences.zh: 監視中官高起潛招致之，不往。

translations.literal: Supervising eunuch Gao Qiqian tried to summon him, but he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising eunuch Gao Qiqian tried to summon him, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 中以他事，落職。

translations.literal: The eunuch on another matter stripped him of his post.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch later had him dismissed on another charge.

sentences.zh: 用一藻薦，復官，及是死難。

translations.literal: Through Yizao’s recommendation he was restored to office, and on this occasion died in the line of duty.
translations.idiomatic: Yizao recommended him back to office, and on this mission he died in service.

sentences.zh: 振從父國柱，崇禎九年為宣府總兵官。

translations.literal: Zhen’s uncle Guozhu, in the ninth year of Chongzhen became regional commander of Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen’s uncle Guozhu became regional commander of Xuanfu in the ninth year of Chongzhen (1636).

sentences.zh: 十一年冬，入衛畿輔，從總督盧象升戰賈莊。

translations.literal: In the winter of the eleventh year he entered the capital region to reinforce the metropolitan defense, and followed Grand Coordinator Lu Xiangsheng in battle at Jiazhuang.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the eleventh year he marched into the metropolitan defense zone and fought with Grand Coordinator Lu Xiangsheng at Jiazhuang.

sentences.zh: 象升敗歿，國柱當坐罪。

translations.literal: Xiangsheng was defeated and perished; Guozhu should have been punished for it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangsheng was killed in defeat; Guozhu was liable to punishment.

sentences.zh: 大學士劉宇亮、侍郎孫傳庭皆言其身入重圍，非臨敵退卻者比。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Liu Yuliang and Vice Minister Sun Chuanting both said that he had entered a heavy encirclement and was not comparable to one who retreats before the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Liu Yuliang and Vice Minister Sun Chuanting both argued that he had been caught in a heavy encirclement and was not like a commander who flees before the enemy.

sentences.zh: 乃充為事官，戴罪圖功。

translations.literal: He was therefore made an officer on probation, bearing guilt while seeking merit.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore reduced to probationary status, to serve on sufferance while seeking merit.

sentences.zh: 十四年，祖大壽被困錦州，總督洪承疇率八大將往救。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, when Zu Dashi was trapped at Jinzhou, Grand Coordinator Hong Chengchou led the eight great generals to relieve him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year (1641), when Zu Dashi was besieged at Jinzhou, Grand Coordinator Hong Chengchou led eight major generals to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 國柱先至松山，陷伏中。

translations.literal: Guozhu arrived first at Songshan and fell into an ambush.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhu reached Songshan first and walked into an ambush.

sentences.zh: 大清兵四面呼降，國柱太息，語其下曰：「此吾兄子昔年殉難處也，吾獨為降將軍乎！」

translations.literal: Great Qing troops on four sides called for surrender; Guozhu sighed deeply and said to his men: "This is where my elder brother’s son died for the cause years ago—shall I alone become a surrendering general?"
translations.idiomatic: Qing troops on all sides shouted for surrender; Guozhu sighed and told his men, "This is where my brother’s son died years ago—am I to be the general who surrenders?"

sentences.zh: 突圍，中矢墮馬卒。

translations.literal: He broke out of the encirclement, was struck by an arrow, fell from his horse, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He charged out of the encirclement, was hit by an arrow, fell from his horse, and died.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈恤如制。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, posthumous condolence was granted according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous honors were granted according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 國柱二子俱夭。

translations.literal: Guozhu’s two sons both died young.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhu’s two sons both died in childhood.

sentences.zh: 妻何氏以所遺甲胄弓矢及戰馬五十三匹獻諸朝。

translations.literal: His wife Lady He presented to the court the armor, bow and arrows, and fifty-three war horses he had left.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, Lady He, presented to the court the armor, bows, arrows, and fifty-three war horses he had left.

sentences.zh: 帝深嘉嘆，命授一品夫人，有司月給米石，餼之終身。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply praised and sighed over this, ordered her made a first-rank lady, and commanded the authorities to give her monthly rations of grain and stipend for life.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply moved, made her a lady of the first rank, and ordered the authorities to supply her with monthly grain and stipend for life.

sentences.zh: 曹變蛟，文詔從子也，幼從文詔積軍功至遊擊。

translations.literal: Cao Bianjiao was a nephew of Wen Zhao; in youth he followed Wen Zhao and through accumulated military merit reached mobile corps commander.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Bianjiao was the nephew of Cao Wenzhao; as a youth he followed Wenzhao and rose through accumulated military merit to mobile corps commander.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年從復河曲。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongzhen he followed in recovering Hequ.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chongzhen (1631) he took part in recovering Hequ.

sentences.zh: 明年連破賊紅軍友等於張麻村、隴安、水落城、唐毛山，又破劉道江等於銅川橋，勇冠諸軍。

translations.literal: The next year he in succession broke the bandit Hong Junyou and others at Zhangmacun, Long’an, Shuiluocheng, and Tangmaoshan, and again broke Liu Daojiang and others at Tongchuan Bridge; his courage topped all the armies.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he routed the bandits Hong Junyou and others at Zhangmacun, Long’an, Shuiluocheng, and Tangmaoshan, and Liu Daojiang and others at Tongchuan Bridge—his valor was unmatched in the army.

sentences.zh: 以御史吳甡薦，進參將。

translations.literal: On the recommendation of Censor Wu Shen he was promoted to vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: On Censor Wu Shen’s recommendation he was promoted to vice commander.

sentences.zh: 文詔移山西，變蛟從戰輒勝。

translations.literal: When Wenzhao was transferred to Shanxi, Bianjiao followed him in battle and each time won.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzhao was transferred to Shanxi, Bianjiao campaigned with him and won repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 及文詔改鎮大同，山西巡撫許鼎臣言：「晉賊紫金梁雖死，老回回、過天星、大天王、蠍子塊、闖塌天諸渠未滅。

translations.literal: When Wenzhao was reassigned to command Datong, Shanxi Grand Coordinator Xu Dingchen said: "Though the Jin bandit Zijin Liang is dead, the chieftains Old Huihui, Guo Tianxing, Great Heavenly King, Scorpion Lump, and Chuang Tietian are not yet destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzhao was reassigned to command Datong, Shanxi Grand Coordinator Xu Dingchen wrote: "Though the Shanxi bandit Zijin Liang is dead, the chieftains Old Huihui, Guo Tianxing, Great Heavenly King, Scorpion Lump, and Chuang Tietian are still at large.

sentences.zh: 變蛟驍勇絕人，麾下健兒千百，才乃文詔亞，乞留之晉中。」

translations.literal: Bianjiao’s fierce courage surpasses other men; under his command are hundreds of stalwart warriors; his talent is only second to Wenzhao—I beg to keep him in Jin."
translations.idiomatic: Bianjiao’s daring is unrivaled and he has hundreds of crack troops under him; his ability is second only to Wenzhao’s—I beg that he be kept in Shanxi."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 七年，群賊入湖廣，命變蛟南征。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, when the mass of bandits entered Huguang, Bianjiao was ordered to campaign south.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (1634), when large bandit forces entered Huguang, Bianjiao was ordered south.

sentences.zh: 文詔困於大同，又命北援。

translations.literal: Wenzhao was hard pressed at Datong, and [Bianjiao] was again ordered to reinforce the north.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao was in difficulties at Datong and Bianjiao was ordered north again to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 七月遇大清兵廣武，有戰功。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he met Great Qing troops at Guangwu and had merit in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he fought Qing forces at Guangwu with success.

sentences.zh: 其冬，文詔失事論戍，變蛟亦以疾歸。

translations.literal: That winter Wenzhao was condemned and sent into exile for his failure; Bianjiao also returned home on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Wenzhao was condemned and banished for his defeat; Bianjiao also went home on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 明年，文詔起討陜西賊，變蛟以故官從。

translations.literal: The next year Wenzhao was raised again to suppress the Shaanxi bandits, and Bianjiao followed in his former office.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Wenzhao was recalled to suppress the Shaanxi bandits, and Bianjiao rejoined him in his former rank.

sentences.zh: 大捷金嶺川，鏖真寧之湫頭鎮，皆為軍鋒。

translations.literal: Great victories at Jinlingchuan and bitter fighting at Zhenning’s Qiutou Fort—on each occasion he was the army’s spearhead.
translations.idiomatic: He won a great victory at Jinlingchuan and fought fiercely at Qiutou Fort in Zhenning—each time at the head of the army.

sentences.zh: 文詔既戰歿，變蛟收潰卒，復成一軍。

translations.literal: After Wenzhao died in battle, Bianjiao gathered the scattered troops and re-formed an army.
translations.idiomatic: After Wenzhao fell in battle, Bianjiao rallied the broken troops and formed a new army.

sentences.zh: 總督洪承疇薦為副總兵，置麾下，與高傑破賊關山鎮，逐北三十餘里。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Hong Chengchou recommended him as vice commander and placed him under his command; with Gao Jie he broke the bandits at Guanshan Fort and pursued them north more than thirty li.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Hong Chengchou recommended him as vice commander and kept him under his command; with Gao Jie he routed bandits at Guanshan Fort and pursued them more than thirty li north.

sentences.zh: 又與副將尤翟文、遊擊孫守法追闖王高迎祥，與戰鳳翔官亭，斬首七百余級。

translations.literal: Again with Vice Commander You Zhaowen and Mobile Corps Commander Sun Shoufa he pursued the Chuang King Gao Yingxiang and fought at Guanting in Fengxiang, beheading more than seven hundred.
translations.idiomatic: With Vice Commander You Zhaowen and Mobile Corps Commander Sun Shoufa he pursued the Chuang King Gao Yingxiang and fought at Guanting in Fengxiang, taking more than seven hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 又與總兵左光先敗迎祥乾州。

translations.literal: Again with Regional Commander Zuo Guangxian he defeated Yingxiang at Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: With Regional Commander Zuo Guangxian he defeated Yingxiang at Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 迎祥中箭走，斬首三百五十余級。

translations.literal: Yingxiang was struck by an arrow and fled; more than three hundred fifty heads were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Yingxiang was wounded by an arrow and fled; more than three hundred fifty heads were taken.

sentences.zh: 已而迎祥自華陰南原絕大嶺，夜出朱陽關。

translations.literal: Before long Yingxiang from south of Huayin crossed the great ridge of the southern plain by night and came out through Zhuyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Yingxiang crossed the great ridge south of Huayin by night and emerged through Zhuyang Pass.

sentences.zh: 光先戰不利，賴變蛟陷陣，乃獲全。

translations.literal: Guangxian fought with ill success; relying on Bianjiao to break the formation, they were only then able to escape whole.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxian’s battle went badly; only when Bianjiao smashed the enemy line were they able to withdraw intact.

sentences.zh: 九年破闖將澄城。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he defeated the Chuang general at Chengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (1636) he defeated a Chuang general at Chengcheng.

sentences.zh: 偕光先等追至靖虜衛，轉戰安定、會寧，抵靜寧、固寧，賊屢挫。

translations.literal: Together with Guangxian and others he pursued to Jingluwei, fought at Anding and Huining, reached Jingning and Guyuan, and the bandits were repeatedly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: With Guangxian and others he pursued them to Jingluwei and fought through Anding, Huining, Jingning, and Guyuan, defeating the bandits again and again.

sentences.zh: 其秋追混天星等，敗之蒲城。

translations.literal: That autumn he pursued Hun Tianxing and others and defeated them at Pucheng.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he pursued Hun Tianxing and others and routed them at Pucheng.

sentences.zh: 賊西走平涼、鞏昌，復擊破之。

translations.literal: The bandits went west toward Pingliang and Gongchang, and he again attacked and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits moved west toward Pingliang and Gongchang, and he defeated them again.

sentences.zh: 十年二月，巡撫孫傳庭部卒許忠叛，勾賊混十萬謀犯西安。

translations.literal: In the second month of the tenth year, Grand Coordinator Sun Chuanting’s troops mutinied under Xu Zhong, who colluded with the bandit Hun Shiwan to plot an attack on Xi’an.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the tenth year (1637), troops under Grand Coordinator Sun Chuanting mutinied under Xu Zhong, who colluded with the bandit Hun Shiwan to strike at Xi’an.

sentences.zh: 變蛟方西追過天星，聞亂急還，賊遂遁。

translations.literal: Bianjiao was pursuing Guo Tianxing in the west; hearing of the disturbance he hurried back, and the bandits thereupon fled.
translations.idiomatic: Bianjiao was pursuing Guo Tianxing in the west; when he heard of the revolt he turned back in haste and the bandits dispersed.

sentences.zh: 傳庭已誅迎祥，其黨闖將混天星、過天星踞洮、岷、階、文深谷間。

translations.literal: Chuanting had already executed Yingxiang; his lieutenants the Chuang generals Hun Tianxing and Guo Tianxing held the deep valleys among Tao, Min, Jie, and Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanting had already executed Yingxiang; his lieutenants the Chuang generals Hun Tianxing and Guo Tianxing held the deep valleys of Tao, Min, Jie, and Wen.

sentences.zh: 承疇遣變蛟、光先及祖大弼、孫顯祖合擊。

translations.literal: Chengchou sent Bianjiao, Guangxian, Zu Dabi, and Sun Xianzu to attack jointly.
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou sent Bianjiao, Guangxian, Zu Dabi, and Sun Xianzu against them together.

sentences.zh: 四月望，入山，遇賊郭家壩，大雨。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth of the fourth month they entered the mountains and met the bandits at Guojiaba in heavy rain.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth of the fourth month they entered the mountains and met the bandits at Guojiaba in a downpour.

sentences.zh: 諸將力戰，賊死傷無算，食盡引還。

translations.literal: The generals fought with all their strength; the bandits died and were wounded beyond counting; their food was exhausted and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The generals fought fiercely; bandit dead and wounded were beyond count; when their provisions ran out they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 九月，階州陷，與光先並停俸。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Jiezhou fell, and Bianjiao and Guangxian both had their salaries suspended.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Jiezhou fell, and both Bianjiao and Guangxian had their salaries suspended.

sentences.zh: 俄擢都督僉事，為臨洮總兵官。

translations.literal: Shortly he was promoted to Regional Military Commissioner and made regional commander of Lintao.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to Regional Military Commissioner and appointed regional commander of Lintao.

sentences.zh: 當是時，承疇、傳庭共矢滅賊。

translations.literal: At that time Chengchou and Chuanting together vowed to exterminate the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Chengchou and Chuanting were united in vowing to exterminate the bandits.

sentences.zh: 傳庭戰於東，承疇戰於西，東賊幾盡。

translations.literal: Chuanting fought in the east and Chengchou in the west; the eastern bandits were nearly all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanting fought in the east and Chengchou in the west, and the eastern bandits were nearly wiped out.

sentences.zh: 賊在西者，復由階、成出西和、禮縣。

translations.literal: The bandits in the west again came out from Jie and Cheng into Xihe and Lixian.
translations.idiomatic: The western bandits broke out again through Jie and Cheng into Xihe and Lixian.

sentences.zh: 光先、顯祖皆無功，獨變蛟降小紅狼。

translations.literal: Guangxian and Xianzu both had no merit; only Bianjiao made Little Red Wolf surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxian and Xianzu achieved nothing; only Bianjiao induced Little Red Wolf to surrender.

sentences.zh: 余賊竄走徽州、兩當、成、鳳間，不敢大逞。

translations.literal: The remaining bandits fled into the region between Huizhou, Liangdang, Cheng, and Feng, and did not dare show themselves on a large scale.
translations.idiomatic: The rest scattered among Huizhou, Liangdang, Cheng, and Feng and no longer dared operate openly.

sentences.zh: 十月，賊間蜀中虛，陷寧羌州，分三道，連陷三十余州縣。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, the bandits, seeing Shu weak, took Ningqiang Prefecture and divided into three columns, in succession taking more than thirty prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the bandits, finding Sichuan undefended, seized Ningqiang Prefecture and in three columns overran more than thirty prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 承疇率變蛟等由沔縣歷寧羌，過七盤、朝天二關。

translations.literal: Chengchou led Bianjiao and others from Mianxian through Ningqiang, passing the two passes of Qipan and Chaotian.
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou led Bianjiao and others from Mianxian through Ningqiang and over the Qipan and Chaotian passes.

sentences.zh: 山高道狹，士馬饑疲，歲暮抵廣元，賊已走還秦。

translations.literal: The mountains were high and the roads narrow; men and horses were hungry and weary; at year’s end they reached Guangyuan, but the bandits had already fled back to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: The mountains were high and the roads narrow; men and horses were exhausted; by year’s end they reached Guangyuan, but the bandits had already retreated into Qin.

sentences.zh: 變蛟等回軍邀擊，斬首五百余級。

translations.literal: Bianjiao and others turned back the army to intercept and strike, cutting off more than five hundred heads.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march Bianjiao and others ambushed the bandits and took more than five hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 時兵部尚書楊嗣昌創「四正六隅」之說，限三月平賊。

translations.literal: At that time Minister of War Yang Sichang devised the doctrine of the "Four Fronts and Six Corners," limiting [the campaign] to three months to pacify the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Minister of War Yang Sichang devised the "Four Fronts and Six Corners" plan, giving three months to pacify the bandits.

sentences.zh: 十一年四月以滅賊逾期，普議降罰，變蛟、光先並鐫五級，戴罪辦賊。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eleventh year, because exterminating the bandits had passed the deadline, there was general deliberation on demotion and punishment; Bianjiao and Guangxian were both reduced five grades and bore guilt while pursuing the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the eleventh year (1638), because the deadline for destroying the bandits had passed, Bianjiao and Guangxian were each demoted five grades and ordered to pursue the bandits under penalty.

sentences.zh: 賊之再入秦也，其渠魁號六隊者，與大天王、混天王、爭管王四部連營東犯，混天星、過天星二部仍伏階、文，獨闖將李自成以三月自洮州出番地。

translations.literal: When the bandits again entered Qin, their chieftain called the Six Columns, together with the Great Heavenly King, the Mixed Heavenly King, and the Contending Manager King’s four divisions, joined camps and invaded east; the Mixed Heaven Star and Guo Tianxing’s two divisions still lay hidden in Jie and Wen, while the Chuang general Li Zicheng alone in the third month came out of the Tibetan country from Taozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits re-entered Qin, their leader the Six Columns, with the Great Heavenly King, Mixed Heavenly King, and Contending Manager King in four allied columns, marched east; Mixed Heaven Star and Guo Tianxing still held Jie and Wen, while the Chuang general Li Zicheng alone left Taozhou into Tibetan territory in the third month.

sentences.zh: 承疇令變蛟偕賀人龍追之，連戰斬首六千七百有奇。

translations.literal: Chengchou ordered Bianjiao together with He Renlong to pursue him; in successive battles more than six thousand seven hundred heads were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou sent Bianjiao with He Renlong in pursuit; in a series of battles they took more than six thousand seven hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 番地乏食，賊多死亡。

translations.literal: In the Tibetan country food was scarce and many bandits died.
translations.idiomatic: Food was scarce in the Tibetan country and many bandits perished.

sentences.zh: 變蛟轉戰千里，身不解甲者二十七晝夜。

translations.literal: Bianjiao fought for a thousand li, not removing his armor for twenty-seven days and nights.
translations.idiomatic: Bianjiao fought for a thousand li without removing his armor for twenty-seven days and nights.

sentences.zh: 余賊潰入塞。

translations.literal: The remaining bandits broke and entered the frontier passes.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors broke through into the frontier passes.

sentences.zh: 大弼駐洮州，扼戰不力。

translations.literal: Dabi garrisoned Taozhou but fought with ill effect at the choke point.
translations.idiomatic: Dabi held Taozhou but failed to block them effectively.

sentences.zh: 乃走入岷州及西和、禮縣山中。

translations.literal: [The bandits] then ran into the mountains of Minzhou and of Xihe and Lixian.
translations.idiomatic: They fled into the mountains of Minzhou, Xihe, and Lixian.

sentences.zh: 變蛟還剿，賊伏匿不敢出，惟六隊勢猶張。

translations.literal: Bianjiao returned to suppress them; the bandits lay hidden and did not dare come out—only the Six Columns’ force was still strong.
translations.idiomatic: Bianjiao returned to hunt them down; the bandits hid and dared not emerge—only the Six Columns still held power.

sentences.zh: 六月，光先自固原進兵，賊已奔隴州、清水。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Guangxian advanced from Guyuan, but the bandits had already fled to Longzhou and Qingshui.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Guangxian advanced from Guyuan, but the bandits had already run to Longzhou and Qingshui.

sentences.zh: 光先追至秦州，六隊及爭管王復走成縣、階州，為變蛟所扼。

translations.literal: Guangxian pursued to Qinzhou; the Six Columns and the Contending Manager King again fled to Chengzhou and Jiezhou and were blocked by Bianjiao.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxian pursued to Qinzhou; the Six Columns and Contending Manager King fled again to Chengzhou and Jiezhou, where Bianjiao blocked them.

sentences.zh: 其別部號三隊及仁義王、混天王降於光先，而自成、六隊及其黨祁總管避秦兵，復謀犯蜀，副將馬科、賀人龍拒之。

translations.literal: Their separate division called the Three Columns and the Benevolence and Righteousness King and Mixed Heavenly King surrendered to Guangxian, while Zicheng, the Six Columns, and their follower Qi the Supervisor, avoiding Qin troops, again plotted to invade Shu; Vice Commander Ma Ke and He Renlong barred them.
translations.idiomatic: A separate band called the Three Columns, with the Benevolence and Righteousness King and Mixed Heavenly King, surrendered to Guangxian; Zicheng, the Six Columns, and their follower Supervisor Qi, evading Qin forces, plotted again to invade Sichuan, but Vice Commanders Ma Ke and He Renlong barred the way.

sentences.zh: 將還走階、文及西鄉，憚變蛟，乃走漢中，又為光先所扼。

translations.literal: About to return, they fled through Jie, Wen, and Xixiang; fearing Bianjiao, they then went to Hanzhong and were again blocked by Guangxian.
translations.idiomatic: Turning back through Jie, Wen, and Xixiang, they feared Bianjiao and made for Hanzhong, where Guangxian blocked them again.

sentences.zh: 六隊、祁總管皆降，惟自成東遁。

translations.literal: The Six Columns and Supervisor Qi all surrendered; only Zicheng fled east.
translations.idiomatic: The Six Columns and Supervisor Qi surrendered; only Zicheng escaped east.

sentences.zh: 承疇令變蛟窮追，而設三覆於潼關之南原。

translations.literal: Chengchou ordered Bianjiao to pursue to the end and set three ambushes on the southern plain of Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou ordered Bianjiao to pursue relentlessly and laid three ambushes on the southern plain at Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 變蛟追及，大呼斫賊。

translations.literal: Bianjiao caught up and shouted to cut down the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Bianjiao caught up and shouted for the men to cut down the bandits.

sentences.zh: 伏盡起，賊屍相枕藉。

translations.literal: The ambushes all rose; bandit corpses lay pillow to pillow.
translations.idiomatic: The ambushes sprang up and bandit dead lay in heaps.

sentences.zh: 村民用大棒擊逃者。

translations.literal: Villagers used great clubs to strike those who fled.
translations.idiomatic: Villagers beat the fugitives with heavy clubs.

sentences.zh: 自成妻女俱失，從七騎遁去。

translations.literal: Zicheng’s wife and daughters were both lost; he fled away with seven horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng lost his wife and daughters and fled with only seven horsemen.

sentences.zh: 余皆降。

translations.literal: All the rest surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: All the rest surrendered.

sentences.zh: 是時，曹兵最強，各鎮依之以為固，錄關中平賊功，進變蛟左都督。

translations.literal: At that time Cao’s troops were strongest; each garrison relied on them as a support; recording the merit of pacifying bandits in Guanzhong, Bianjiao was advanced to Left Chief Regional Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Cao’s troops were the strongest in the field and other commands relied on them; for pacifying the bandits in Guanzhong, Bianjiao was promoted to Left Chief Regional Military Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十一月，京師戒嚴，召承疇入衛，變蛟及光先從之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the capital was placed on alert; Chengchou was summoned to reinforce the capital, and Bianjiao and Guangxian followed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the capital went on alert; Chengchou was recalled to defend it, and Bianjiao and Guangxian marched with him.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，抵近畿，帝遣使迎勞，將士各有賜。

translations.literal: In the second month of the next year they reached the near metropolitan region; the emperor sent envoys to welcome and comfort them, and officers and soldiers each received gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The following second month they reached the metropolitan approaches; the emperor sent envoys to welcome them and rewarded officers and men.

sentences.zh: 未幾，戰渾河，無功。

translations.literal: Before long they fought at the Hun River without merit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward they fought at the Hun River without success.

sentences.zh: 再戰太平砦北，小有斬獲。

translations.literal: Again they fought north of Taiping Fort and had a small taking of heads.
translations.idiomatic: They fought again north of Taiping Fort with minor gains.

sentences.zh: 及解嚴，留屯遵化。

translations.literal: When the alert was lifted they remained garrisoned at Zunhua.
translations.idiomatic: When the emergency ended they were left at Zunhua.

sentences.zh: 麾下皆秦卒，思歸，多逃亡者，追斬之乃定。

translations.literal: Under their command were all Qin soldiers who longed to return home; many fled, and only after pursuit and execution were they settled.
translations.idiomatic: Their troops were all Shaanxi men who longed for home; many deserted and had to be hunted down and executed before order was restored.

sentences.zh: 時張獻忠、羅汝才既降復叛，陜西再用兵。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Xianzhong and Luo Rucai had surrendered and rebelled again, and Shaanxi was again under arms.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xianzhong and Luo Rucai had surrendered and rebelled again, and Shaanxi was mobilized once more.

sentences.zh: 總督鄭崇儉乞令變蛟兵西還，帝不許，尋用為東協總兵官。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Zheng Chongjian begged that Bianjiao’s troops be sent back west; the emperor did not permit it, and soon afterward [Bianjiao] was made eastern cooperative regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Zheng Chongjian asked that Bianjiao’s army be sent west again; the emperor refused, and soon made him eastern cooperative regional commander.

sentences.zh: 十三年五月，錦州告急。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the thirteenth year Jinzhou reported urgent danger.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the thirteenth year (1640) Jinzhou reported an emergency.

sentences.zh: 從總督承疇出關，駐寧遠。

translations.literal: He followed Grand Coordinator Chengchou out of the pass and garrisoned Ningyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Grand Coordinator Chengchou through the pass and encamped at Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 七月與援剿總兵左光先、山海總兵馬科、寧遠總兵吳三桂、遼東總兵劉肇基，遇大清兵於黃土臺及松山、杏山，互有殺傷。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, together with relief-and-suppression commander Zuo Guangxian, Shanhai commander Ma Ke, Ningyuan commander Wu Sangui, and Liaodong commander Liu Zhaoji, he met Great Qing troops at Huangtutai and at Songshan and Xingshan, with mutual killing and wounding.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, with relief commander Zuo Guangxian, Shanhai commander Ma Ke, Ningyuan commander Wu Sangui, and Liaodong commander Liu Zhaoji, he met Qing forces at Huangtutai, Songshan, and Xingshan with heavy casualties on both sides.

sentences.zh: 大清兵退屯義州。

translations.literal: Great Qing troops withdrew and encamped at Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing withdrew to Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 承疇議遣變蛟、光先、科之兵入關養銳，留三桂、肇基於松、杏間，佯示進兵狀。

translations.literal: Chengchou deliberated sending the troops of Bianjiao, Guangxian, and Ke inside the pass to rest their edge, leaving Sangui and Zhaoji between Song and Xing to feign a show of advancing.
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou proposed sending Bianjiao, Guangxian, and Ke’s troops inside the pass to recover their strength, while Sangui and Zhaoji remained between Songshan and Xingshan to feign an advance.

sentences.zh: 又請解肇基任，代以王廷臣；

translations.literal: He also asked to relieve Zhaoji of his post and replace him with Wang Tingchen;
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to replace Zhaoji with Wang Tingchen;

sentences.zh: 遣光先西歸，代以白廣恩。

translations.literal: he sent Guangxian back west and replaced him with Bai Guangen.
translations.idiomatic: he sent Guangxian west and brought in Bai Guangen in his place.

sentences.zh: 部議鹹從之，而請調旁近邊軍，合關內外見卒十五萬人備戰守。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated and all followed this, but requested transferring nearby frontier armies, combining inside and outside the pass the troops presently under arms—one hundred fifty thousand men—to prepare for battle and defense.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry approved but asked to draw in nearby frontier armies so that inside and outside the pass there would be one hundred fifty thousand men ready for battle and defense.

sentences.zh: 用承疇言，師行糧從，必芻糧足支一歲，然後可議益兵。

translations.literal: Following Chengchou’s words: when the army moves, provisions follow—it must be that fodder and grain suffice for one year, and only then may one discuss increasing troops.
translations.idiomatic: Following Chengchou’s argument that an army cannot march without a year’s fodder and grain in hand before more troops could be added.

sentences.zh: 帝然之，敕所司速措給。

translations.literal: The emperor approved this and ordered the relevant offices to supply quickly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and ordered the offices to provision them at once.

sentences.zh: 征宣府總兵楊國柱、大同總兵王樸、密雲總兵唐通各揀精兵赴援。

translations.literal: Regional commanders Yang Guozhu of Xuanfu, Wang Pu of Datong, and Tang Tong of Miyun each picked elite troops to go to the relief.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commanders Yang Guozhu of Xuanfu, Wang Pu of Datong, and Tang Tong of Miyun each selected elite troops for the relief.

sentences.zh: 以十四年三月偕變蛟、科、廣恩先後出關，合三桂、廷臣凡八大將，兵十三萬，馬四萬，並駐寧遠。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourteenth year Bianjiao, Ke, and Guangen in succession went out of the pass; together with Sangui and Tingchen there were eight great generals, one hundred thirty thousand soldiers and forty thousand horses, all encamped at Ningyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourteenth year (1641) Bianjiao, Ke, and Guangen marched out of the pass in turn; with Sangui and Tingchen there were eight commanders, one hundred thirty thousand infantry and forty thousand horses, all at Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 承疇主持重，而朝議以兵多餉艱，職方郎張若麒趣戰。

translations.literal: Chengchou held to caution, but court opinion, because troops were many and rations difficult, [and] the Bureau Director Zhang Ruolin urged battle.
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou favored caution, but the court, finding the army costly to feed, and Bureau Director Zhang Ruolin pressing for battle.

sentences.zh: 承疇念祖大壽被圍久，乃議急救錦州。

translations.literal: Chengchou, mindful that Zu Dashi had long been besieged, then deliberated on urgently relieving Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful that Zu Dashi had been besieged for so long, Chengchou resolved to relieve Jinzhou at once.

sentences.zh: 七月二十八日，諸軍次松山，營西北岡。

translations.literal: On the twenty-eighth day of the seventh month the armies halted at Songshan and encamped on the northwest ridge.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-eighth of the seventh month the armies reached Songshan and camped on the northwest ridge.

sentences.zh: 數戰，圍不解。

translations.literal: After several battles the siege was not lifted.
translations.idiomatic: After several engagements the siege was not broken.

sentences.zh: 八月，國柱戰歿，以山西總兵李輔明代之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Guozhu died in battle; Shanxi commander Li Fuming was made to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Guozhu was killed in battle and Shanxi commander Li Fuming replaced him.

sentences.zh: 承疇命變蛟營松山之北，乳峰山之西，兩山間列七營，環以長壕。

translations.literal: Chengchou ordered Bianjiao to encamp north of Songshan and west of Rufeng Mountain, with seven camps ranged between the two mountains, ringed by a long moat.
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou placed Bianjiao north of Songshan and west of Rufeng Mountain, with seven camps between the two peaks and a long trench around them.

sentences.zh: 俄聞我太宗文皇帝親臨督陣，諸將大懼。

translations.literal: Shortly it was heard that Our Taizong Wen Emperor came in person to oversee the array; the generals were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Soon word came that the Qing Taizong Emperor Wen had come in person to direct the battle; the generals were terrified.

sentences.zh: 及出戰，連敗，餉道又絕。

translations.literal: When they went out to battle they were repeatedly defeated, and the supply route was also cut.
translations.idiomatic: They went out to fight and were beaten again and again, and their supply lines were cut.

sentences.zh: 樸先夜遁。

translations.literal: Pu fled by night first.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was the first to flee by night.

sentences.zh: 通、科、三桂、廣恩、輔明相繼走。

translations.literal: Tong, Ke, Sangui, Guangen, and Fuming in succession ran away.
translations.idiomatic: Tong, Ke, Sangui, Guangen, and Fuming fled one after another.

sentences.zh: 自杏山迤南沿海，東至塔山，為大清兵邀擊，溺海死者無算。

translations.literal: From Xingshan south along the coast east to Tashan, Great Qing troops intercepted them; those drowned in the sea were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: From Xingshan south along the coast to Tashan the Qing intercepted them; countless men drowned in the sea.

sentences.zh: 變蛟、廷臣聞敗，馳至松山，與承疇固守。

translations.literal: Bianjiao and Tingchen, hearing of the defeat, galloped to Songshan and with Chengchou held firm in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the rout, Bianjiao and Tingchen raced to Songshan and held on with Chengchou.

sentences.zh: 三桂、樸奔據杏山。

translations.literal: Sangui and Pu fled to hold Xingshan.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui and Pu fell back to Xingshan.

sentences.zh: 越數日，欲走還寧遠。

translations.literal: After several days they wished to flee back to Ningyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After several days they tried to break back to Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 至高橋遇伏，大敗，僅以身免。

translations.literal: At Gaoqiao they met an ambush, were greatly defeated, and barely escaped with their lives.
translations.idiomatic: At Gaoqiao they were ambushed and routed, escaping only with their lives.

sentences.zh: 先後喪士卒凡五萬三千七百余人。

translations.literal: In all they successively lost fifty-three thousand seven hundred odd soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In all they lost fifty-three thousand seven hundred odd troops.

sentences.zh: 自是錦州圍益急，而松山亦被圍，應援俱絕矣。

translations.literal: From this the Jinzhou siege grew all the more urgent, while Songshan was also besieged and all relief was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the siege of Jinzhou tightened, Songshan was surrounded, and all relief was cut off.

sentences.zh: 九月，承疇、變蛟等盡出城中馬步兵，欲突圍出，敗還。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Chengchou, Bianjiao, and others sent out all the cavalry and infantry in the city, wishing to break out, but were defeated and driven back.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Chengchou and Bianjiao sent out every horse and foot soldier in the city to break out, but were beaten back.

sentences.zh: 守半年，至明年二月，副將夏成德為內應，松山遂破。

translations.literal: They defended half a year; until the second month of the next year Vice Commander Xia Chengde acted as insider, and Songshan was then taken.
translations.idiomatic: They held half a year; in the second month of the following year Vice Commander Xia Chengde turned traitor and Songshan fell.

sentences.zh: 承疇、變蛟、廷臣及巡撫丘民仰，故總兵祖大樂，兵備道張鬥、姚恭、王之楨，副將江翥、饒勛、朱文德，參將以下百余人皆被執見殺，獨承疇與大樂獲免。

translations.literal: Chengchou, Bianjiao, Tingchen, and Grand Coordinator Qiu Minyang, former commander Zu Dale, defense officials Zhang Dou, Yao Gong, and Wang Zhiji, vice commanders Jiang Zhu, Rao Xun, and Zhu Wende, and vice commanders and below—more than one hundred men—all were captured and killed; only Chengchou and Dale were spared.
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou, Bianjiao, Tingchen, Grand Coordinator Qiu Minyang, former commander Zu Dale, defense officials Zhang Dou, Yao Gong, and Wang Zhiji, vice commanders Jiang Zhu, Rao Xun, and Zhu Wende, and more than a hundred officers down to vice commander were captured and killed; only Chengchou and Dale were spared.

sentences.zh: 文德，義州衛人，後家錦州。

translations.literal: Wende was a man of Yizhou Guard; later his family dwelt at Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wende was a native of Yizhou Guard; his family later settled at Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 崇禎時，積功至松山副將。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen reign through accumulated merit he reached vice commander at Songshan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chongzhen he rose through merit to vice commander at Songshan.

sentences.zh: 忤監視中官高起潛，為所中，斥罷。

translations.literal: He offended the supervising eunuch Gao Qiqian and was slandered by him and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He offended the supervising eunuch Gao Qiqian, who denounced him and had him dismissed.

sentences.zh: 十一年起故官。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 及城被圍，領前鋒拒守甚力，城破竟死。

translations.literal: When the city was besieged he led the vanguard and resisted with great force; when the city fell he died in the end.
translations.idiomatic: When the city was besieged he led the vanguard and fought stubbornly; when it fell he died at his post.

sentences.zh: 三月，大壽遂以錦州降。

translations.literal: In the third month Dashi then surrendered Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Dashi surrendered Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 杏山、塔山連失，京師大震。

translations.literal: Xingshan and Tashan fell in succession; the capital was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Xingshan and Tashan fell in turn and the capital was shaken.

sentences.zh: 詔賜諸臣祭葬，有司建祠。

translations.literal: An edict granted sacrificial burial to the ministers; the authorities built shrines.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted state sacrifices and burials and ordered shrines built.

sentences.zh: 變蛟妻高氏以贈蔭請，乃贈榮祿大夫、太子少保，世蔭錦衣指揮僉事。

translations.literal: Bianjiao’s wife Lady Gao on the basis of posthumous enrollment begged; he was then granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with hereditary enrollment as assistant commander in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Bianjiao’s wife Lady Gao petitioned on his posthumous honors; he was granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with hereditary rank as assistant commander in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 法司會鞫王樸罪。

translations.literal: The judicial offices jointly tried Wang Pu’s crime.
translations.idiomatic: The judicial offices jointly tried Wang Pu.

sentences.zh: 御史郝晉言：「六鎮罪同，皆宜死。

translations.literal: Censor Hao Jin said: "The guilt of the six commands is the same—all ought to die.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Hao Jin argued: "The six commands are equally guilty and all deserve death.

sentences.zh: 三桂實遼左主將，不戰而逃，奈何反加提督？」

translations.literal: Sangui was in fact the chief general of eastern Liao; he did not fight and fled—why on the contrary was he promoted to grand coordinator?"
translations.idiomatic: Sangui was the chief commander in Liaodong; he fled without fighting—why was he promoted to grand coordinator instead?"

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書陳新甲覆議，請獨斬樸，勒科軍令狀，再失機即斬決。

translations.literal: Minister of War Chen Xin Jia replied in deliberation, asking that only Pu be beheaded, that Ke’s military pledge be recorded, and that on another failure he be executed at once.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Chen Xin Jia replied that only Pu should be executed, that Ke be bound by military law to be executed on the next failure.

sentences.zh: 三桂失地應斬，念守寧遠功，與輔明、廣恩、通皆貶秩，充為事官。

translations.literal: Sangui for losing territory ought to be beheaded; mindful of his merit in defending Ningyuan, together with Fuming, Guangen, and Tong he was all reduced in rank and made officers on probation.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui deserved death for abandoning his post, but in view of his defense of Ningyuan he, with Fuming, Guangen, and Tong, was demoted and reduced to probationary status.

sentences.zh: 輔明，遼東人，累官副總兵。

translations.literal: Fuming was a man of Liaodong and through successive offices reached vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: Fuming was a native of Liaodong and rose to vice commander.

sentences.zh: 崇禎八年從祖寬擊賊，連蹙之嵩縣、汝州、確山。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Chongzhen he followed Zu Kuan in striking bandits and in succession pressed them at Songxian, Ruzhou, and Queshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Chongzhen he followed Zu Kuan against bandits and drove them through Songxian, Ruzhou, and Queshan.

sentences.zh: 明年追破賊於滁州。

translations.literal: The next year he pursued and broke the bandits at Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he routed bandits at Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 敘功，加都督僉事。

translations.literal: When merit was recorded he was given Regional Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was made Regional Military Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十二年擢山西總兵官，被劾罷。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was promoted to Shanxi regional commander but was impeached and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was made Shanxi regional commander but was impeached and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 明年從承疇出關，使代國柱，竟敗。

translations.literal: The next year he followed Chengchou out of the pass and was made to replace Guozhu, but in the end was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he followed Chengchou through the pass to replace Guozhu and was defeated in the end.

sentences.zh: 十六年為援剿總兵。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was made relief-and-suppression commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he became relief-and-suppression commander.

sentences.zh: 是冬，大清兵薄寧遠，輔明馳援，軍敗猶力戰，歿於陣。

translations.literal: That winter Great Qing troops pressed Ningyuan; Fuming galloped to relieve it; the army was defeated but he still fought with force and perished in the array.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Qing forces threatened Ningyuan; Fuming rode to relieve it; his army was beaten but he fought on and died in the line.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈特進榮祿大夫、左都督，世蔭錦衣副千戶，賜祭葬，列壇前屯祀之。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was posthumously granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Left Chief Regional Military Commissioner, hereditary enrollment as vice thousand-household in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard, sacrificial burial granted, and enshrined at the altar before Qiantun.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Left Chief Regional Military Commissioner, hereditary vice thousand-household in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard, state burial, and a shrine before Qiantun.

sentences.zh: 樸，榆林衛人。

translations.literal: Pu was a man of Yulin Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was a native of Yulin Guard.

sentences.zh: 父威，官左都督，九佩將印，為提鎮者五十年。

translations.literal: His father Wei held office as Left Chief Regional Military Commissioner; nine times he wore a general’s seal and for fifty years was a commander or regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wei was Left Chief Regional Military Commissioner, bore nine general’s seals, and for fifty years held command or regional command.

sentences.zh: 兄世欽，裏居殉難，見《尤世威傳》中。

translations.literal: His elder brother Shiqin, living in retirement, died for the cause—see the biography of You Shiwei.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Shiqin, in retirement, died for the cause—see the biography of You Shiwei.

sentences.zh: 樸由父蔭屢遷京營副將。

translations.literal: Pu through his father’s enrollment was repeatedly promoted to vice commander in the capital garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Pu rose through his father’s privilege to vice commander in the capital armies.

sentences.zh: 崇禎六年，賊躪畿南，命樸與倪寵為總兵官，將京軍六千，監以中官楊應朝、盧九德，屢有斬獲功，進右都督。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Chongzhen, when bandits trampled the south of the capital region, Pu was ordered together with Ni Chong to be regional commander, leading six thousand capital troops supervised by eunuchs Yang Yingchao and Lu Jiude; they repeatedly had merit in cutting off heads and he was advanced to Right Chief Regional Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Chongzhen, when bandits ravaged the metropolitan south, Pu and Ni Chong were made regional commanders with six thousand capital troops under eunuchs Yang Yingchao and Lu Jiude; they won repeated victories and Pu was promoted to Right Chief Regional Military Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 明年代曹文詔鎮大同，進左都督。

translations.literal: The next year he replaced Cao Wenzhao in command of Datong and was advanced to Left Chief Regional Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he replaced Cao Wenzhao as commander of Datong and was made Left Chief Regional Military Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 九年秋，都城被兵，詔樸入衛，賚蟒衣彩幣，竟無功。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the ninth year the capital was attacked by troops; an edict ordered Pu to enter and defend; python robes and colored silks were bestowed, but in the end there was no merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the ninth year (1636) the capital was attacked; Pu was ordered to reinforce it and given python robes and silks, but achieved nothing.

sentences.zh: 十一年加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was given Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 是冬，從總督盧象升入衛，方戰欒城、束鹿間。

translations.literal: That winter he followed Grand Coordinator Lu Xiangsheng into the capital defense and was just fighting between Luancheng and Shulu.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he followed Grand Coordinator Lu Xiangsheng to defend the capital and was fighting between Luancheng and Shulu.

sentences.zh: 或言大同有警即引兵歸。

translations.literal: Some said that if Datong had an alarm he would at once lead his troops back.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor had it that he would march home at the first alarm from Datong.

sentences.zh: 及是救錦州，以首逃下詔獄。

translations.literal: When on this occasion he went to relieve Jinzhou, because he was the first to flee he was placed in the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: When he marched to relieve Jinzhou he was the first to flee and was thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 十五年五月伏誅。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifteenth year he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fifteenth year (1642) he was executed.

sentences.zh: 科，起偏裨至大帥，戰功亞變蛟，與三桂同守寧遠有功。

translations.literal: Ke, from partial officer to great commander, had battle merit second to Bianjiao; together with Sangui he defended Ningyuan with merit.
translations.idiomatic: Ke rose from a junior officer to full command; his battle record was second only to Bianjiao’s, and with Sangui he had merit defending Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 十六年春，督兵入衛，賜宴武英殿，命從大學士吳甡南征，不果行。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixteenth year he supervised troops entering the capital defense; a feast was given at the Hall of Martial Glory; he was ordered to follow Grand Secretary Wu Shen on the southern campaign, but in the end did not go.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixteenth year (1643) he led troops to the capital, was feasted in the Hall of Martial Glory, and was ordered to follow Wu Shen south—but never went.

sentences.zh: 明年三月從李建泰西征。

translations.literal: In the third month of the next year he followed Li Jiantai on the western expedition.
translations.idiomatic: The next March he followed Li Jiantai on the western expedition.

sentences.zh: 李自成兵至，科遂降，封懷仁伯。

translations.literal: When Li Zicheng’s troops arrived, Ke then surrendered and was enfeoffed as Earl of Huairen.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zicheng’s army arrived Ke surrendered and was made Earl of Huairen.

sentences.zh: 廣恩，初從混天猴為盜。

translations.literal: Guangen at first followed Mixed Heaven Monkey as a bandit.
translations.idiomatic: Guangen had first served the bandit Mixed Heaven Monkey.

sentences.zh: 既降，屢立戰功。

translations.literal: After he surrendered he repeatedly had merit in battle.
translations.idiomatic: After surrendering he won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 松山敗還，代馬科鎮山海關。

translations.literal: When Songshan was defeated he returned and replaced Ke as commander of Shanhai Pass.
translations.idiomatic: After the Songshan disaster he returned and replaced Ke as commander of Shanhai Pass.

sentences.zh: 是年十一月，京師戒嚴，廣恩入衛，賚銀幣羊酒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of that year the capital was on alert; Guangen entered to defend and was given silver, silks, sheep, and wine.
translations.idiomatic: That November the capital went on alert; Guangen marched in and was rewarded with silver, silks, sheep, and wine.

sentences.zh: 俄戰龍王口，稍有斬獲，以捷聞。

translations.literal: Shortly he fought at Longwangkou and had a small taking of heads; victory was reported.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he fought at Longwangkou with minor gains and reported a victory.

sentences.zh: 帝始惡廣恩觀望，降旨譙責，而冀其後效，特命敘功。

translations.literal: The emperor at first disliked Guangen’s watching and waiting, sent down an edict of rebuke, yet still hoped for later effect and specially ordered his merit recorded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor first resented Guangen’s hesitation, rebuked him by edict, yet still hoped for better service and ordered his merits recorded.

sentences.zh: 明年四月合八鎮兵戰螺山，悉潰敗。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the next year he joined the eight commands in battle at Luoshan and was utterly routed.
translations.idiomatic: The next April he joined eight commands at Luoshan and was utterly routed.

sentences.zh: 總督趙光抃請帝召之入，用為武經略。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Zhao Guangbian asked the emperor to summon him in and employed him as military intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Zhao Guangbian asked the emperor to recall him and made him military intendant.

sentences.zh: 廣恩以帝頻戮大將，己又多過，懼不敢至，假索餉名，頓真定。

translations.literal: Guangen, because the emperor frequently executed great generals and he himself had many faults, feared and did not dare come; under the pretext of requesting rations he halted at Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Guangen, knowing the emperor was executing generals and conscious of his own faults, dared not come; he halted at Zhending on the pretext of collecting pay.

sentences.zh: 大學士吳甡將南征，密請帝嚴旨逮治，而己力救，率之剿寇。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Wu Shen was about to campaign south and secretly asked the emperor for a stern edict to arrest and punish him, while he himself exerted force to save him and led him to suppress bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shen, about to campaign south, secretly asked for a stern arrest order while himself intervening to save Guangen and lead him against bandits.

sentences.zh: 廣恩感甚。

translations.literal: Guangen was deeply moved.
translations.idiomatic: Guangen was deeply grateful.

sentences.zh: 無何，帝遣中官賫二萬金犒其軍，且諭以溫旨。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor sent a eunuch bearing twenty thousand in gold to comfort his army and also conveyed warm words.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the emperor sent a eunuch with twenty thousand taels to reward his army and spoke encouraging words.

sentences.zh: 廣恩遂驕，不為甡用，大掠臨洺關，徑歸陜西。

translations.literal: Guangen then grew arrogant, would not obey Shen, greatly plundered Linming Pass, and went straight back to Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Guangen then grew arrogant, refused Shen’s orders, plundered Linming Pass, and marched straight back to Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 帝不得已，命隸督師孫傳庭辦賊。

translations.literal: The emperor had no choice and ordered him placed under Commander Sun Chuanting to pursue bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had no choice but to place him under Commander Sun Chuanting to fight bandits.

sentences.zh: 十月，郟縣師覆，加廣恩蕩寇將軍，俾緣道收潰卒以保潼關。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the army at Yingxian was destroyed; Guangen was given the title Bandit-Suppressing General and ordered along the route to gather broken troops to hold Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the army at Yingxian was destroyed; Guangen was named Bandit-Suppressing General and told to gather fugitives along the road to hold Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 未幾，潼關亦破，廣恩西奔固原。

translations.literal: Before long Tong Pass also fell; Guangen fled west to Guyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Tong Pass fell too; Guangen fled west to Guyuan.

sentences.zh: 賊將追躡及之，即開門降。

translations.literal: Bandit generals pursued and caught up with him; he at once opened the gates and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit pursuers caught him at Guyuan; he opened the gates and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 自成大喜，握手共飲，封桃源伯。

translations.literal: Zicheng was greatly pleased, clasped his hand and drank with him together, and enfeoffed him as Earl of Taoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng rejoiced, drank with him hand in hand, and made him Earl of Taoyuan.

sentences.zh: 通，口辯無勇略。

translations.literal: Tong was glib in speech and without courage or strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Tong was eloquent but lacked courage and strategy.

sentences.zh: 既敗歸，仍鎮密雲。

translations.literal: After he was defeated and returned he still commanded Miyun.
translations.idiomatic: After his defeat he still held Miyun.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，奉詔入衛，命守禦三河、平谷。

translations.literal: That winter he received an edict to enter the capital defense and was ordered to defend Sanhe and Pinggu.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was ordered to reinforce the capital and defend Sanhe and Pinggu.

sentences.zh: 大清兵下山東，通尾之而南，抵青州，迄不敢一戰。

translations.literal: Great Qing troops descended on Shandong; Tong followed at their rear and went south to Qingzhou, yet to the end did not dare fight once.
translations.idiomatic: Qing troops overran Shandong; Tong trailed them south to Qingzhou and never offered battle.

sentences.zh: 明年復尾而北，戰螺山，敗績。

translations.literal: The next year he again followed north and fought at Luoshan with a record of defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he followed north again and was beaten at Luoshan.

sentences.zh: 已，命從甡南征。

translations.literal: Afterward he was ordered to follow Shen on the southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He was then ordered to follow Shen south.

sentences.zh: 甡未行而斥，乃令通轄薊鎮西協。

translations.literal: Before Shen had set out he was dismissed, and Tong was ordered to command the western cooperative of Jizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was dismissed before marching; Tong was given the western cooperative of Jizhen.

sentences.zh: 五月汰密雲總兵官，命兼轄中協四路。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the Miyun regional command was abolished; he was ordered also to command the four routes of the central cooperative.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Miyun command was abolished and he was given the four routes of the central cooperative as well.

sentences.zh: 尋用孔希貴於西協，而命通專轄中協。

translations.literal: Shortly Kong Xigui was used in the western cooperative while Tong was ordered to command only the central cooperative.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Kong Xigui took the western cooperative and Tong held only the central.

sentences.zh: 十月，關外有警，命率師赴援，以銀牌二百為賞功用。

translations.literal: In the tenth month there was an alarm outside the passes; he was ordered to lead troops to relieve it, with two hundred silver tokens as reward for merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month there was an alarm beyond the passes; he was ordered to relieve it with two hundred silver tokens promised for merit.

sentences.zh: 事定，復移鎮西協。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he was again transferred to command the western cooperative.
translations.idiomatic: When the crisis passed he was moved back to the western cooperative.

sentences.zh: 帝顧通厚，有蟒衣玉帶之賜，召見稱卿而不名，錫之宴，獎勞備至。

translations.literal: The emperor regarded Tong with favor; there were gifts of python robes and jade belts; on audience he was called “minister” without naming him; feasts were granted; rewards and comfort were complete.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor favored Tong lavishly—python robes, jade belts, audiences where he was addressed as “minister” without his name, feasts and unstinting praise.

sentences.zh: 明年，賊逼宣府，命移守居庸，封定西伯。

translations.literal: The next year, when bandits pressed Xuanfu, he was ordered to move and defend Juyong and was enfeoffed as Earl of Dingxi.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when bandits threatened Xuanfu, he was shifted to Juyong and made Earl of Dingxi.

sentences.zh: 無何，賊犯關，即偕中官杜之秩迎降，京師遂陷。

translations.literal: Before long bandits attacked the passes; he at once together with eunuch Du Zhiji went out to welcome surrender, and the capital was then taken.
translations.idiomatic: Soon bandits breached the passes; he and eunuch Du Zhiji went out to surrender, and the capital fell.

sentences.zh: 光先，梟將也，與賊角陜西，功最多。

translations.literal: Guangxian was a fierce general; contending with bandits in Shaanxi, his merit was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxian was a fierce commander whose record against Shaanxi bandits was the greatest.

sentences.zh: 自遼左遣還，廢不用。

translations.literal: From Liao he was sent back and discarded without employment.
translations.idiomatic: Sent back from Liaodong, he was left unused.

sentences.zh: 後聞廣恩從賊，亦詣賊降。

translations.literal: Later, hearing that Guangen had followed the bandits, he also went to the bandits and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Later, learning Guangen had joined the rebels, he too went over and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 又有陳永福者，守開封，射李自成中目。

translations.literal: There was also Chen Yongfu, who defended Kaifeng and shot Li Zicheng in the eye.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Chen Yongfu, who held Kaifeng and shot Li Zicheng in the eye.

sentences.zh: 及自成陷山西，令廣恩諭之降。

translations.literal: When Zicheng took Shanxi he ordered Guangen to urge him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Zicheng overran Shanxi he sent Guangen to offer surrender.

sentences.zh: 永福懼誅，意猶豫。

translations.literal: Yongfu feared execution and still hesitated.
translations.idiomatic: Yongfu feared death and hesitated.

sentences.zh: 自成折箭以示信，乃降，封為文水伯。

translations.literal: Zicheng broke an arrow to show good faith; [Yongfu] then surrendered and was enfeoffed as Earl of Wenshui.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng broke an arrow as a pledge of faith; Yongfu then surrendered and was made Earl of Wenshui.

sentences.zh: 後自成敗還山西，永福為守太原，殺晉府宗室殆盡。

translations.literal: Later when Zicheng was defeated and returned to Shanxi, Yongfu held Taiyuan and killed nearly all the princes of the Jin imperial house.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Zicheng retreated to Shanxi, Yongfu held Taiyuan and killed nearly every member of the Jin imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 劉肇基，字鼎維，遼東人。

translations.literal: Liu Zhaoji, style Dingwei, was a man of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhaoji, courtesy name Dingwei, was a native of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 嗣世職指揮僉事，遷都司僉書，隸山海總兵官尤世威麾下。

translations.literal: He inherited the hereditary office of assistant commander, was promoted to Assistant Commander in the Chief Military Commission, and served under Shanhai regional commander You Shiwei.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited an assistant commandership, rose to Assistant Commander in the Chief Military Commission, and served under Shanhai commander You Shiwei.

sentences.zh: 崇禎七年從世威援宣府，又從剿中原賊。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Chongzhen he followed Shiwei to relieve Xuanfu and again followed in suppressing bandits in the central plains.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Chongzhen (1634) he followed Shiwei to relieve Xuanfu and then campaigned against central-plain bandits.

sentences.zh: 進遊擊，戍雒南蘭草川。

translations.literal: He was promoted to mobile corps commander and garrisoned Lancao in Luonan.
translations.idiomatic: He was made mobile corps commander and garrisoned Lancao on the Luonan Lancao River.

sentences.zh: 明年遇賊，戰敗傷臂。

translations.literal: The next year he met bandits and was defeated in battle with an injured arm.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he met bandits in battle, was beaten, and wounded his arm.

sentences.zh: 未幾，世威罷，肇基及遊擊羅岱分將其兵，與祖寬大破賊汝州，斬首千六百有奇。

translations.literal: Before long Shiwei was dismissed; Zhaoji and mobile corps commander Luo Dai divided his troops; with Zu Kuan they greatly broke the bandits at Ruzhou and cut off more than one thousand six hundred heads.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shiwei was dismissed; Zhaoji and Luo Dai split his army; with Zu Kuan he routed bandits at Ruzhou and took more than sixteen hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 後從寬數有功，而其部下皆邊軍，久戍思歸，與寬軍噪而走。

translations.literal: Afterward he followed Kuan with repeated merit, but his subordinates were all frontier troops who long garrisoned and longed to return; with Kuan’s army they mutinied and ran off.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Kuan with further victories, but his men were frontier troops weary of garrison duty; they mutinied with Kuan’s force and deserted.

sentences.zh: 總理盧象升乃遣之入秦。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Lu Xiangsheng then sent them into Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Lu Xiangsheng sent them into Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 其秋，畿輔有警，始還山海，竟坐前罪解職，令從征自效。

translations.literal: That autumn there was an alarm in the metropolitan region; he first returned to Shanhai; in the end he was punished for the earlier offense, dismissed from office, and ordered to follow campaigns to redeem himself.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the capital region was threatened; he returned to Shanhai, was punished for the mutiny and dismissed, and ordered to earn reinstatement in the field.

sentences.zh: 俄以固守永平功復職，屢遷遼東副總兵。

translations.literal: Shortly, on the merit of firmly holding Yongping, he was restored to office and repeatedly promoted to Liaodong vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, for holding Yongping, he was restored and promoted repeatedly to Liaodong vice commander.

sentences.zh: 十二年冬，薊遼總督洪承疇請用為署總兵官，分練寧遠諸營卒。

translations.literal: In the winter of the twelfth year Jizhou-Liaodong Grand Coordinator Hong Chengchou asked to use him as acting regional commander to drill separately the troops of the Ningyuan camps.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the twelfth year Grand Coordinator Hong Chengchou asked to make him acting regional commander to train the Ningyuan garrisons.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書傅宗龍稍持之，帝怒，下宗龍獄，擢肇基都督僉事任之。

translations.literal: Minister of War Fu Zonglong slightly held back the appointment; the emperor was angry, placed Zonglong in prison, and promoted Zhaoji to Regional Military Commissioner to take the post.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Fu Zonglong hesitated; the emperor was furious, imprisoned Zonglong, and promoted Zhaoji to Regional Military Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，錦州有警。

translations.literal: In the third month of the next year Jinzhou reported an alarm.
translations.idiomatic: The next third month Jinzhou reported an emergency.

sentences.zh: 承疇命吳三桂偕肇基赴松山為聲援。

translations.literal: Chengchou ordered Wu Sangui together with Zhaoji to go to Songshan as a supporting force.
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou sent Wu Sangui with Zhaoji to Songshan as reinforcement.

sentences.zh: 三桂困松、杏間，肇基救出之，喪士卒千人。

translations.literal: Sangui was trapped between Song and Xing; Zhaoji rescued him and lost one thousand soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui was trapped between Songshan and Xingshan; Zhaoji rescued him at the cost of a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 七月與曹變蛟等戰黃土臺及松山、杏山。

translations.literal: In the seventh month together with Cao Bianjiao and others he fought at Huangtutai and at Songshan and Xingshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he fought with Cao Bianjiao and others at Huangtutai, Songshan, and Xingshan.

sentences.zh: 九月，復戰杏山，肇基軍稍卻。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he again fought at Xingshan; Zhaoji’s army retreated somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he fought again at Xingshan and his line gave ground.

sentences.zh: 承疇甄別諸將，解肇基職，代以王廷臣。

translations.literal: Chengchou sifted the generals, relieved Zhaoji of his post, and replaced him with Wang Tingchen.
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou reviewed the commanders, removed Zhaoji, and replaced him with Wang Tingchen.

sentences.zh: 十七年春，加都督同知，提督南京大教場，及福王立，史可法督師淮、揚，肇基請從征自效。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventeenth year he was given Chief Regional Military Commissioner and made superintendent of the great training ground at Nanjing; when the Prince of Fu was established, Shi Kefa supervised the Huai-Yang front, and Zhaoji asked to follow the campaign to redeem himself.
