translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventeenth year (1644) he was made Chief Regional Military Commissioner and superintendent of Nanjing’s great training ground; when the Prince of Fu was enthroned and Shi Kefa took command on the Huai-Yang front, Zhaoji volunteered.

sentences.zh: 屢加左都督、太子太保。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly given Left Chief Regional Military Commissioner and Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Left Chief Regional Military Commissioner and Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 可法議分布諸將，奏薦李成棟、賀大成、王之綱、李本身、胡茂楨為總兵官。

translations.literal: Kefa deliberated on distributing the generals and memorialized recommending Li Chengdong, He Dacheng, Wang Zhiji, Li Benshen, and Hu Maozhen as regional commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Kefa planned the deployment and recommended Li Chengdong, He Dacheng, Wang Zhiji, Li Benshen, and Hu Maozhen as regional commanders.

sentences.zh: 成棟鎮徐州，大成揚州，之綱開封。

translations.literal: Chengdong garrisoned Xuzhou, Dacheng Yangzhou, Zhiji Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Chengdong held Xuzhou, Dacheng Yangzhou, Zhiji Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 本身、茂楨隸高傑麾下，為前鋒。

translations.literal: Benshen and Maozhen were under Gao Jie’s command as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Benshen and Maozhen served under Gao Jie as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 而令肇基駐高家集，李樓鳳駐睢寧，以防河。

translations.literal: Zhaoji was ordered to garrison Gaojiaji and Li Loufeng Suining to guard the river.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoji was posted at Gaojiaji and Li Loufeng at Suining to guard the river.

sentences.zh: 棲鳳本甘肅總兵，以地失留淮、揚間也。

translations.literal: Loufeng had originally been Gansu regional commander and remained in the Huai-Yang region because his territory was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Loufeng had been Gansu regional commander and stayed in Huai-Yang after losing his province.

sentences.zh: 閣標前鋒，則用張天祿駐瓜洲。

translations.literal: For the vanguard of the river standard, Zhang Tianlu was posted at Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tianlu was stationed at Guazhou as river vanguard.

sentences.zh: 十一月，肇基、棲鳳以可法命謀取宿遷。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Zhaoji and Loufeng on Kefa’s orders planned to recover Suqian.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Zhaoji and Loufeng, on Kefa’s orders, planned to retake Suqian.

sentences.zh: 初八日渡河，復其城。

translations.literal: On the eighth of the first month they crossed the river and recovered the city.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth they crossed the river and retook the city.

sentences.zh: 越數日，大清兵圍邳州，軍城北，肇基軍城南，相持半月，大清兵引去。

translations.literal: After several days Great Qing troops besieged Pizhou; the army was north of the city and Zhaoji’s army south of the city; they faced each other half a month and Great Qing troops withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Days later Qing forces besieged Pizhou; Loufeng held the north and Zhaoji the south; after half a month the Qing withdrew.

sentences.zh: 順治二年三月，大清兵抵揚州，可法邀諸將赴援。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Shunzhi Great Qing troops reached Yangzhou; Kefa invited the generals to come to the relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Shunzhi year 2 (1645) Qing troops reached Yangzhou and Kefa called the generals to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 獨肇基自白洋河趨赴，過高郵不見妻子。

translations.literal: Only Zhaoji from Baiyang River hurried to the rescue; passing Gaoyou he did not see his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zhaoji hurried from Baiyang River, passing Gaoyou without stopping for his family.

sentences.zh: 既入城，請乘大清兵未集，背城一戰。

translations.literal: After he entered the city he asked, while Great Qing troops were not yet gathered, to fight with his back to the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Once inside he urged a battle with the city at their backs before the Qing concentrated.

sentences.zh: 可法持重，肇基乃分守北門，發炮傷圍者。

translations.literal: Kefa was cautious; Zhaoji then divided forces to defend the north gate and fired cannon wounding those besieging.
translations.idiomatic: Kefa was cautious; Zhaoji took the north gate and shelled the besiegers.

sentences.zh: 已而城破，率所部四百人巷戰，格殺數百人。

translations.literal: Before long the city fell; he led his four hundred men in street fighting and killed several hundred in close combat.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he led four hundred men in street fighting and killed hundreds in close combat.

sentences.zh: 後騎來益眾，力不支，一軍皆沒。

translations.literal: Later horsemen came in ever greater numbers; strength could not be sustained and the whole army perished.
translations.idiomatic: More cavalry poured in; overwhelmed, his entire command perished.

sentences.zh: 副將乙邦才、馬應魁、莊子固等皆同死。

translations.literal: Vice commanders Yi Bangcai, Ma Yingkui, Zhuang Zigu, and others all died together.
translations.idiomatic: Vice commanders Yi Bangcai, Ma Yingkui, Zhuang Zigu, and others died with him.

sentences.zh: 乙邦才，青州人。

translations.literal: Yi Bangcai was a man of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Bangcai was a native of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中，以隊長擊賊於河南、江北間。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen reign, as a squad leader he struck bandits between Henan and the north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chongzhen, as a squad leader he fought bandits in Henan and north Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 大將黃得功與賊戰霍山，單騎逐賊，陷淖中。

translations.literal: Great general Huang Degong fought bandits at Huoshan; alone on horseback he pursued bandits and fell into a mire.
translations.idiomatic: General Huang Degong fought bandits at Huoshan; chasing alone he rode into a bog.

sentences.zh: 賊圍而射之，馬斃，得功徒步鬥。

translations.literal: Bandits surrounded him and shot; his horse died; Degong fought on foot.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits surrounded and shot him; his horse died and he fought on foot.

sentences.zh: 天將暮，僅余二矢。

translations.literal: Heaven was about to grow dark; only two arrows remained.
translations.idiomatic: Dusk was falling and he had only two arrows left.

sentences.zh: 邦才大呼沖賊走，得功乃得出。

translations.literal: Bangcai shouted loudly and charged the bandits, who fled; Degong was then able to get out.
translations.idiomatic: Bangcai charged the bandits with a shout and they scattered; Degong escaped.

sentences.zh: 邦才授以己馬，分矢與之，且走且射，殪追騎十余人，始得及其軍。

translations.literal: Bangcai gave him his own horse, divided arrows with him, and while running and shooting killed more than ten pursuing horsemen before at last rejoining the army.
translations.idiomatic: Bangcai gave him his horse, shared his arrows, and while retreating shot down more than ten pursuers before rejoining the army.

sentences.zh: 得功自是知邦才。

translations.literal: From this Degong came to know Bangcai.
translations.idiomatic: From that day Degong knew Bangcai’s worth.

sentences.zh: 時有張衡者，亦以驍敢名。

translations.literal: At that time there was also Zhang Heng, famed likewise for fierce daring.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Zhang Heng, famed for equal daring.

sentences.zh: 賊圍六安急，總督馬士英救之。

translations.literal: Bandits urgently besieged Lu’an; Grand Coordinator Ma Shiying went to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu’an was hard pressed, Grand Coordinator Ma Shiying marched to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 甫至，斥其左右副將，而號於軍中曰：「孰為乙邦才、張衡者？」

translations.literal: Just as he arrived he dismissed his left and right vice commanders and cried in the army: "Who are Yi Bangcai and Zhang Heng?"
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he dismissed his vice commanders and shouted through the camp, "Which of you are Yi Bangcai and Zhang Heng?"

sentences.zh: 兩人入謁，即牒補副將，以其兵授之，曰：「為我入六安，取知州狀來報。」

translations.literal: The two men entered to pay respects; he at once issued documents supplementing them as vice commanders, gave them his troops, and said: "For me enter Lu’an and bring back the prefect’s report."
translations.idiomatic: They came forward; he made them vice commanders on the spot, gave them his troops, and said, "Enter Lu’an and bring me the prefect’s report."

sentences.zh: 兩人出，即簡精騎二百，夜沖賊陣而入，繞城大呼，曰：「大軍至矣，固守勿懈！」

translations.literal: The two went out, at once picked two hundred elite horsemen, and by night charged into the bandit array; circling the city they shouted loudly: "The great army has arrived—hold firm and do not slacken!"
translations.idiomatic: They chose two hundred elite horsemen, charged the bandit lines by night, and circled the walls crying, "The main army is here—hold firm!"

sentences.zh: 城中人喜，守益堅。

translations.literal: The people in the city rejoiced and the defense grew all the firmer.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison took heart and held all the firmer.

sentences.zh: 兩人促知州署狀，復奪圍出，不損一騎。

translations.literal: The two men urged the prefect to sign a report, again broke through the encirclement and came out, and did not lose a single horseman.
translations.idiomatic: They had the prefect sign a report, broke out again, and returned without losing a man.

sentences.zh: 時潁、壽、六安、霍山諸州縣數被寇，邦才大小十余戰，鹹有功。

translations.literal: At that time the prefectures and counties of Ying, Shou, Lu’an, and Huoshan were repeatedly harried by bandits; Bangcai in more than ten battles large and small all had merit.
translations.idiomatic: Ying, Shou, Lu’an, and Huoshan were repeatedly raided; Bangcai fought more than ten engagements, large and small, and won each time.

sentences.zh: 及可法鎮揚州，攜之行。

translations.literal: When Kefa garrisoned Yangzhou he took [Bangcai] with him on the march.
translations.idiomatic: When Kefa took command at Yangzhou he brought Bangcai with him.

sentences.zh: 至是戰敗，自刎死。

translations.literal: On this occasion he was defeated in battle and cut his own throat and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the final battle he was defeated and took his own life.

sentences.zh: 馬應魁，字守卿，貴池人。

translations.literal: Ma Yingkui, style Shouqing, was a man of Guichi.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yingkui, courtesy name Shouqing, was a native of Guichi.

sentences.zh: 初為小將，率家丁五十人巡村落間。

translations.literal: At first a junior officer, he led fifty household retainers patrolling among the villages.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a junior officer leading fifty household retainers on village patrols.

sentences.zh: 猝遇賊，眾懼欲奔。

translations.literal: Suddenly they met bandits; the crowd feared and wished to flee.
translations.idiomatic: They suddenly met bandits; his men panicked and wanted to run.

sentences.zh: 應魁大聲曰：「勿怖死！

translations.literal: Yingkui said in a loud voice: "Do not fear death!
translations.idiomatic: Yingkui shouted, "Do not fear death!

sentences.zh: 死，命也。」

translations.literal: Death is fate."
translations.idiomatic: Death is fate."

sentences.zh: 連發二矢殪二賊，賊即退。

translations.literal: In succession he shot two arrows and killed two bandits; the bandits at once withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He loosed two arrows and killed two bandits, and they withdrew at once.

sentences.zh: 可法因拔為副總兵，俾領旗鼓。

translations.literal: Kefa therefore pulled him up to vice commander and made him lead the standards and drums.
translations.idiomatic: Kefa made him vice commander and put him in charge of the standards.

sentences.zh: 每戰披白甲，大書「盡忠報國」四字於背，至是巷戰死。

translations.literal: In each battle he wore white armor and wrote large on his back the four characters "Utmost Loyalty in Serving the State"; on this occasion he died in street fighting.
translations.idiomatic: In every battle he wore white armor with "Serve the state with utmost loyalty" written large on his back; he died fighting in the streets at Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 莊子固，字憲伯，遼東人，年十三，殺人亡命。

translations.literal: Zhuang Zigu, style Xianbo, was a man of Liaodong; at age thirteen he killed a man and fled for his life.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang Zigu, courtesy name Xianbo, was a native of Liaodong who at thirteen killed a man and fled.

sentences.zh: 後從軍有功，積官至參將。

translations.literal: Later he followed the army with merit and through accumulated offices reached vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: He later entered the army, won distinction, and rose to vice commander.

sentences.zh: 嘗從山西總兵許定國救開封，軍半道噪歸，定國獲罪。

translations.literal: He once followed Shanxi regional commander Xu Dingguo to relieve Kaifeng; the army halfway mutinied and returned; Dingguo was punished.
translations.idiomatic: He once followed Shanxi commander Xu Dingguo to relieve Kaifeng; the army mutinied halfway home and Dingguo was punished.

sentences.zh: 子固輯余眾，得免議。

translations.literal: Zigu gathered the remaining troops and was able to avoid censure.
translations.idiomatic: Zigu rallied the remnants and escaped blame.

sentences.zh: 後可法出鎮，用為副總兵，俾興屯於徐州、歸德間。

translations.literal: Later when Kefa went out to command, [Zigu] was used as vice commander and made to open military colonies between Xuzhou and Guide.
translations.idiomatic: When Kefa took the field he made Zigu vice commander and set him to open military colonies between Xuzhou and Guide.

sentences.zh: 子固募壯士七百人，以赤心報國為號。

translations.literal: Zigu recruited seven hundred stalwarts and took as their motto "Loyal Hearts Repaying the State.
translations.idiomatic: Zigu raised seven hundred stalwarts under the banner "Loyal Hearts for the State.

sentences.zh: 聞揚州被圍，率眾馳救，三日而至。

translations.literal: Hearing Yangzhou was besieged, he led his crowd in a gallop to relieve it and arrived in three days.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard Yangzhou was besieged he marched to its relief and arrived in three days.

sentences.zh: 城將破，欲擁可法出城，遇大清兵，格鬥死。

translations.literal: The city was about to fall; he wished to embrace Kefa and take him out of the city; he met Great Qing troops and died in close combat.
translations.idiomatic: As the city was falling he tried to escort Kefa out, met Qing troops, and died fighting.

sentences.zh: 他若副將樓挺、江雲龍、李豫，參將陶國祚、許謹、馮國用、陳光玉、李隆、徐純仁，遊擊李大忠、孫開忠，都司姚懷龍、解學曾等十余人，皆以巷戰死。

translations.literal: Others such as vice commanders Lou Ting, Jiang Yunlong, and Li Yu, vice commanders Tao Guozuo, Xu Jin, Feng Guoyong, Chen Guangyu, Li Long, and Xu Chunren, mobile corps commanders Li Dazhong and Sun Kaizhong, and bureau directors Yao Huailong and Xie Xuezeng—more than ten men—all died in street fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Vice commanders Lou Ting, Jiang Yunlong, and Li Yu; colonels Tao Guozuo, Xu Jin, Feng Guoyong, Chen Guangyu, Li Long, and Xu Chunren; mobile corps commanders Li Dazhong and Sun Kaizhong; and directors Yao Huailong and Xie Xuezeng—more than a dozen officers—all died in the streets.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：金國鳳之善守，曹變蛟之力戰，均無愧良將材。

translations.literal: The appraising comment says: Jin Guofeng’s skill in defense and Cao Bianjiao’s power in battle both were without shame as material for good generals.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Jin Guofeng’s defense and Cao Bianjiao’s fighting both mark them as generals of the first rank.

sentences.zh: 然而運移事易，難於建功，而易於挫敗，遂至謀勇兼絀，以身殉之。

translations.literal: Yet when fortune shifted and affairs changed, it was hard to achieve merit and easy to meet defeat; they reached the point where strategy and courage were both exhausted and they gave their bodies for the cause.
translations.idiomatic: Yet as fortune turned it grew harder to win and easier to lose; strategy and courage alike failed, and they gave their lives for the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 蓋天命有歸，莫之為而為者矣。

translations.literal: It is that Heaven’s mandate had a destination—there was none who did it, yet it was done.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven’s mandate had already found its lord—what happened, happened of itself.
